faqs.q: How much does a Mountain Cur cost to buy?
faqs.a: Reputable breeders typically charge $800–$3,000 for a Mountain Cur puppy. Prices vary by breeder reputation, health testing, and lineage. Rescue adoption fees are typically $100–$500 and include vaccinations, neutering, and microchipping.

faqs.q: What is the monthly cost of owning a Mountain Cur?
faqs.a: Budget $150–$300 per month for a Mountain Cur, covering food, preventive vet care, insurance, grooming and supplies. Mid-size breeds sit in the moderate cost range across most ownership categories.

faqs.q: What are the biggest ongoing costs for a Mountain Cur?
faqs.a: The three largest annual expenses are food ($500–900), veterinary care ($400–$1,200 budgeted annually), and pet insurance ($$400–$1,200 per year). Grooming costs are lower for short-coated breeds managed at home.

faqs.q: How much does a Mountain Cur cost in the first year?
faqs.a: Year one costs for a Mountain Cur are significantly higher than subsequent years, typically $2,000–$4,000. This covers the purchase price or adoption fee, initial vet checks, vaccinations, spay/neuter, microchipping, crate, bedding, collar, leads and puppy training classes.

faqs.q: How often should I groom a Mountain Cur?
faqs.a: Mountain Curs need brushing 3–5 times per week, daily during seasonal coat blows. The dense undercoat requires a dedicated undercoat rake, not just a surface slicker brush. Nails should be trimmed every 3–4 weeks. Ears should be checked and cleaned monthly.

faqs.q: Do Mountain Curs shed a lot?
faqs.a: Mountain Curs have seasonal shedding — manageable with a consistent brushing routine.

faqs.q: What grooming tools does a Mountain Cur need?
faqs.a: A slicker brush for surface debris and an undercoat rake for the dense undercoat are both essential. A shedding blade or deshedding tool helps during heavy moult periods. A nail grinder is useful if your Mountain Cur is sensitive to clippers.

faqs.q: How often should I bathe a Mountain Cur?
faqs.a: Every 4–6 weeks is appropriate for most Mountain Curs that live indoors. More frequent bathing is needed if they swim or spend time in mud. Over-bathing strips natural skin oils — use a pH-balanced dog shampoo rather than human products.

faqs.q: Are Mountain Curs easy to train?
faqs.a: Mountain Curs are moderately easy to train. They respond well to positive reinforcement and benefit from early puppy classes. Consistency from all household members is key.

faqs.q: What training method works best for a Mountain Cur?
faqs.a: Reward-based training using treats, praise and toy rewards is the most effective and well-researched approach for Mountain Curs. Keep sessions short and positive, end on a success, and vary your rewards to maintain engagement.

faqs.q: At what age should I start training my Mountain Cur?
faqs.a: Start training from the day your puppy arrives home, typically at 8 weeks. The 8–16 week window is the most sensitive socialisation period. Enrol in a puppy class within the first two weeks for structured socialisation alongside basic obedience foundations.

faqs.q: How long does it take to train a Mountain Cur?
faqs.a: Most Mountain Curs reliably perform basic cues within 4–6 weeks of daily 10–15 minute sessions. Reliable recall off-lead typically takes 3–4 months of progressive distance and distraction training.

faqs.q: What health problems do Mountain Curs commonly have?
faqs.a: Mountain Curs are most commonly associated with routine age-related conditions. Regular vet checks, appropriate weight management, and breed-specific screening tests help detect issues early. Ask any breeder for health test results before purchasing.

faqs.q: How long do Mountain Curs live?
faqs.a: Mountain Curs have an average lifespan of 10–13 years. Good nutrition, appropriate exercise, weight management and regular vet visits are the key factors in achieving the upper end of this range.

faqs.q: Are Mountain Curs prone to hip dysplasia?
faqs.a: Hip dysplasia is less common in Mountain Curs than in large working breeds, but it can still occur. Responsible breeders screen breeding stock. Keeping your Mountain Cur at a healthy weight is the most effective preventive measure.

faqs.q: What health tests should a Mountain Cur puppy have?
faqs.a: At minimum, your Mountain Cur puppy should have a vet health check, first vaccinations, deworming, and microchipping before coming home. Ask the breeder for parent health certificates relevant to Mountain Cur-specific conditions. A vet check within 72 hours of bringing your puppy home is recommended to establish a baseline.

faqs.q: Are Mountain Curs good with kids?
faqs.a: Mountain Curs can do well with children when properly socialised from puppyhood. Every dog is an individual — early exposure to children's behaviour (noise, sudden movements) is the most effective preparation.

faqs.q: Do Mountain Curs get along with other dogs?
faqs.a: Mountain Curs can be selective with other dogs due to their independent nature. Early socialisation in puppy classes and controlled on-lead introductions with other dogs help build positive associations.

faqs.q: Do Mountain Curs bark a lot?
faqs.a: Mountain Curs tend to be vocal — they may bark at strangers, sounds, or when under-stimulated. Adequate daily exercise and mental enrichment (training sessions, puzzle feeders) significantly reduce nuisance barking. Teaching a "quiet" cue early is worthwhile.

faqs.q: Are Mountain Curs good apartment dogs?
faqs.a: Mountain Curs can live in apartments if their exercise needs are met consistently. The key variable is owner commitment to daily walks and enrichment — breed size alone doesn't determine apartment suitability.

faqs.q: How much exercise does a Mountain Cur need per day?
faqs.a: Mountain Curs need approximately 60–90 minutes of exercise daily. Split across at least two sessions daily, with one higher-intensity session (running, fetch, swimming) and one loose-lead sniff walk. Mental exercise (training sessions, puzzle feeders) counts toward overall stimulation needs and can reduce restless behaviour.

faqs.q: Are Mountain Curs good running partners?
faqs.a: Yes — Mountain Curs make excellent running partners once fully grown (typically 12–18 months for medium breeds, 18–24 months for large breeds). Start with shorter distances and build gradually to protect developing joints.

faqs.q: What happens if a Mountain Cur doesn't get enough exercise?
faqs.a: Under-exercised Mountain Curs often develop destructive behaviours — chewing, digging, excessive barking, and hyperactivity indoors. These are symptoms of frustration, not bad temperament. Two missed exercise sessions back-to-back typically shows up as restlessness or nuisance behaviour.

faqs.q: Can a Mountain Cur be off-lead?
faqs.a: Mountain Curs can be off-lead in secure areas once recall is reliable. Reliable recall typically takes 3–4 months of consistent training with progressive distance and distractions. Never trust off-lead recall in an unfenced area until it's been tested in controlled conditions first.

faqs.q: How much should I feed my Mountain Cur?
faqs.a: A Mountain Cur needs approximately 1½–3 cups of dry food per day for an adult, split across two meals. Always follow the feeding guide on your specific formula — calorie density varies significantly between brands. Adjust portions based on body condition: you should be able to feel (but not easily see) the ribs.

faqs.q: How many times a day should I feed a Mountain Cur?
faqs.a: Adult Mountain Curs should eat twice daily. Puppies (under 6 months) need 3–4 smaller meals per day to support growth and prevent hypoglycaemia, particularly in small breeds.

faqs.q: What is the best food for a Mountain Cur?
faqs.a: Look for a formula carrying an AAFCO adequacy statement for the correct life stage. A named protein source (chicken, turkey, beef, salmon) should appear first in the ingredient list. Active Mountain Curs benefit from higher-protein formulas (26–30% crude protein) to support muscle maintenance.

faqs.q: When should I switch my Mountain Cur from puppy to adult food?
faqs.a: Most Mountain Curs can transition to adult food between 12 and 15 months. Transition gradually over 7–10 days — mix 25% new food with 75% old food and shift the ratio every 2 days to avoid digestive upset.

faqs.q: Is a Mountain Cur a good dog for first-time owners?
faqs.a: Mountain Curs are manageable for motivated first-time owners who research the breed, commit to early training, and have realistic expectations about time and cost.

faqs.q: Are Mountain Curs good family dogs?
faqs.a: Mountain Curs can be excellent family dogs for active households. They thrive with children who can match their energy level. A calm household with limited exercise may not suit this breed's temperament.

faqs.q: Do Mountain Curs do well when left alone?
faqs.a: Mountain Curs form strong bonds with their owners and do not do well with extended isolation. Aim for no more than 4–6 hours alone at a time. If your schedule requires longer absences, consider a dog walker, doggy daycare, or a companion dog.

faqs.q: How much time do you need for a Mountain Cur?
faqs.a: Plan for 2–3 hours per day dedicated to your Mountain Cur — covering exercise, training, feeding and general interaction.  The commitment is consistent year-round, not just when convenient.
